file_rules.why: Every field is read by name, so a renamed or missing column makes every row untrustworthy: reject the whole file.

rules.why: Nothing to settle or trace without them.
PNR is 6 upper-case alphanumerics; 5-character or lower-case values cannot be matched to the booking.
An airline code is 2 characters (digits allowed, e.g. 6E); AIR is not one.
We only settle airlines we have a contract for; XX is well-formed but unknown.
A fare class is one upper-case letter; lower-case k will not match the fare table.
R is one letter but not a class the airline publishes.
OD pair is AAA-BBB; BOMDXB has no separator so origin and destination cannot be split.
Both airports must be known or the route cannot be priced (BOM-XYZ).
Origin equal to destination (BOM-BOM) is not a journey.
More than 2 decimals (4520.555) cannot be paid exactly; reject rather than guess a rounding.
A fare of zero or less (-1200.00) does not belong in an issue file.
INX is not an accepted ISO 4217 code, so the amount has no unit.
Ticket number is a 3-digit prefix, a hyphen and 10 digits; 098-75716779 is short.
The ticket prefix must belong to the airline on the row (125 is British Airways on an Air India row).
ISO dates only; 25/11/2026 is ambiguous (day-first or month-first) so it is not guessed.
A ticket issued after the file's business date (2026-12-25) is not possible.
Valid but more than 30 days old (56 days): keep it in validated/ with a flag so a person can review it.
Agency IATA number is 8 digits; 1234567 cannot identify the agency for settlement.
Same ticket twice in one file: keep the first, skip and count the repeat.
